results.description: a BIF-free recursive list walk on both runtimes (interpreter ns/element)
notes: case list_walk: paired median=1749.963 ms min=1443.602 ms max=1906.430 ms noise=±231.979 ms over 3 round(s)
case list_walk: N=50000 walks (rust) at LEN=1000, i.e. 50000000 elements walked

method: paired startup-cancelled marginal — every round runs the N-walk pass then the 0-walk pass back to back, and ns/element = median(paired difference) / (N * LEN) * 1e6, withheld below 3x max(1 ms, 1.4826*MAD) of the paired differences; N is per runtime so both marginals are measurable, and the fixed process startup (incl. the Rust runtime's code-path resolution) cancels inside every pair; the module is BIF-free and builds no term
note: element count is deterministic and contention-immune; the wall-clock rows move with host load

method: ns/op = median(wall at N ops - wall at 0 ops) / N * 1e6, from interleaved paired rounds (each round runs the N-op sample and then the 0-op sample back to back, so a drifting boot cost cancels inside the pair); N is per runtime so both marginals are measurable, and the fixed process startup (incl. the Rust runtime's code-path resolution) cancels out of every pair; the figure is withheld when the median does not clear the noise band; every case validates its copy round-trip with a bound-variable pattern
note: the op count is deterministic and contention-immune; the wall-clock rows move with host load

budgets.reason: no `cowboy` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The request-tail budget on the I/O-bound target, recorded at 0.11-0.16 ms p99 while serving ~119-124k req/s through a real Cowboy release across the three m19 external reps (m17's contended pass read 3.03-3.59 ms at ~38k req/s): 5 ms leaves room for a loaded host yet still flags a real latency regression; it reads the summary the cowboy row actually records (`latency_ms` — there is no separate p99 metric) and it is sys-only because the Rust runtime cannot boot an OTP release.

The per-element dispatch budget for the standing per-unit gap, recorded at 18.4-18.7 ns/element across the six m19 matched rounds (the oracle reads 2.30-2.34; m17's loaded rounds read up to 48.2): over a hundred times today's figure, so it is a regression alarm for the engine's dispatch path and not a parity target — the gap itself is `beam_engine`'s to close.

The messaging budget for the two-process send/receive round trip, recorded at 6242-6338 ns/op across the six m19 matched rounds (the oracle reads 1487-1531; m17's worst round read 12450): ~3.2x above today's figure and still ~1.6x above m17's worst, so it is a regression alarm rather than a parity target, and it is not a hard ceiling on a contended host.
